predictive_services_discussion: Expect another very hot day across most of the Southern Plains today due to a strong ridge of high pressure. High temperatures in the upper 90s to middle 100s are expected from the eastern half of Texas east to Mississippi. These hot temperatures will combine with relative humidity values ranging from 25-35% across northern Texas and Oklahoma and wind gusts from 20-25 mph resulting in enhanced fire weather conditions. On the periphery of this strong ridge thunderstorms will form from the Desert Southwest northward along the Rockies as well as along the Mid-Atlantic Seaboard and into Florida. These storms will be primarily wet. Another cluster of thunderstorms will develop over the northern Rockies and over extreme northern Washington due to a weak upper-level disturbance. These storms will be a mix of wet and dry. The final area of concern will be Hawaii due to the presence of Tropical Storm Lala. Although the storm will be pushing west of the Islands tonight, wind gusts of 50-60 mph with torrential flooding rains are still expected.
